brief:
Israel's E1 development plan risks bisecting the West Bank, according to Al Jazeera English. The scheme would establish Israeli settlements and infrastructure in a strategic corridor between Jerusalem and the Dead Sea, potentially severing Palestinian territorial continuity and fragmenting the occupied territory.

The E1 area, situated east of Jerusalem, has long been a flashpoint in Israeli-Palestinian disputes over settlement expansion. Palestinian officials and international observers warn that construction there would create a physical barrier cutting the West Bank into disconnected northern and southern sections, complicating Palestinian movement, commerce, and governance.

Advocates of the plan argue it addresses Israeli security and development needs. Critics contend the project would entrench Israeli control over Palestinian land and make a future contiguous Palestinian state increasingly difficult to establish.
dek: Israel's E1 plan risks splitting the West Bank in two.
title: Israel's E1 plan threatens to split West Bank in two
